records.text: Deborah Hertz wrote that the People's Will had 2,193 activists in the 1880s, including 95 Jewish women, who made up almost one third of its 348 women.
records.speaker: Deborah Hertz

appearances.snippet: the people's will attracted 2,193 activists during the decade of the 80s. Among these 2,000, some radicals were 95 Jewish women who represented almost a third of the only 348 women that were in the party.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The numerical comparison is traceable to Deborah Hertz’s published historical analysis: 2,193 activists, 348 women, and 95 Jewish women, making Jewish women more than a quarter of the women in the dataset.

sources.title: Dangerous Politics, Dangerous Liaisons – Deborah Hertz
sources.relevance: Primary scholarly source for the quoted activist and gender counts.

conveyance.original_source: Dangerous Politics, Dangerous Liaisons, Love and Terror Among Jewish Women Radicals in Tsarist Russia

records.text: Deborah Hertz wrote that Jewish women's participation was also robust in the Russian social democratic movement and the social revolutionaries, and connected their attraction to left movements to deteriorating conditions for Russian Jewry.
records.speaker: Deborah Hertz

appearances.snippet: Statistics on the high proportion of Jewish women in the Russian social democratic movement and the social revolutionaries, the successor party to the People's Will, also show a very robust participation by Jewish women. ... When we seek to understand why Jewish women were so attracted to the left movements, we must consider the deteriorating situation of Russian Jewry in these years.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Hertz describes substantial participation by Jewish women in Social Democratic and Socialist Revolutionary activism and connects it to worsening social and legal conditions for Russian Jewry.

sources.title: Dangerous Politics, Dangerous Liaisons – Deborah Hertz
sources.relevance: Supports both participation patterns and the deteriorating conditions discussed.
